bug_semantics: Exported helper setNestedValue (source src/util/object.ts; published as lib/util/object.js) takes a caller-supplied dot-separated path, splits it on '.', and forwards the key array to @antv/util set with no filtering of __proto__, prototype, or constructor. That setter walks keys and does o[key] = value; for a plain target, path __proto__.polluted resolves o to Object.prototype and writes an inherited property, and constructor.prototype.polluted does the same via Function.prototype. Because src/index.ts re-exports src/util (which re-exports object.ts), any consumer that passes untrusted path strings into the public API can pollute Object.prototype (CWE-1321). The CWE-94 label is secondary misclassification of the same sink. Attack is not a built-in remote RCE; it requires the application to feed attacker-controlled path/value into the exported helper.

potential_fix.approach: In setNestedValue, after splitting the path, refuse to process any segment equal to '__proto__', 'prototype', or 'constructor' (or implement a setter that never assigns onto Object.prototype / uses Object.create(null) intermediates).
potential_fix.rationale: The pollution happens because unsanitized path segments are used as object keys in a deep assignment. Blocking those prototype-pollution primitives, or writing only onto non-prototype objects, closes __proto__.polluted and constructor.prototype.polluted before they reach @antv/util set.
